title: Samsung Talks 2020 TV Lineup, Q90R eARC Update, & Why They Don't Support Dolby Vision
description: We interviewed Craig Cunningham, senior product strategy manager for Samsung Europe, talking about the South Korean brand's 2020 TV lineup (including 8K & 4K QLED), eARC firmware update for last year's Q90R television, lack of Dolby Vision support, as well as other lifestyle displays (The Frame, Serif & Sero).  This video was filmed and uploaded in HLG HDR, so please watch on a compatible HDR display for the best experience.  Many thanks to Richer Sounds Manchester for sponsoring this video. If you're thinking about getting a new TV, please support this channel by considering buying from them. Call 0333 900 0086, mention HDTVTest, and you'll receive great price & service.  https://www.richersounds.com/stores/manchester-city-centre  ======================== **Click Below to SUBSCRIBE for More Reviews, Sneak Peeks & Tips: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcCYOO2uYPnG-21WDOWdwew?sub_confirmation=1 ========================  VISIT HDTV Test http://www.hdtvtest.co.uk/  FOLLOW US! https://www.facebook.com/HDTVTest https://twitter.com/hdtvtest https://www.instagram.com/hdtvtest https://twitter.com/vincent_teoh

asr.full_text: This coverage is sponsored by Richesounds Manchester. Call [PHONE] for the best prices and expert advice for TVs, AV and Hi-Fi. Hello everyone, Vincent Teo from HDTVTest here. I'm here in Malta with Mr Craig Cunningham who is the Senior Product Strategy Manager at Samsung Europe. Now, this is not the first time I'm interviewing Craig, but this is certainly the first time I'm doing it when he's at Samsung. So thanks a lot for taking the time to speak to us. No problem. Always a pleasure. And welcome to Samsung Forum. Craig, can you please let us know what are the main themes for Samsung for 2020? Pitch quality continues to be the main focus for us. So we spent a lot of time over the last year developing this lineup. And where we've really focused on is delivering pitch quality,. But in the context of the environment in which the products will be placed. Because I think we often get caught up in specifications,. But actually TVs have to perform in real-world environments and situations. So we've tried to consider all of those external factors. And build a lineup which really can perform regardless of the environment. Where the TV is going to be placed. Can you run through the 2020 lineup for Samsung in terms of televisions then? Sure. So starting from the top, 8K, huge focus. For us. We've expanded the lineup so we now have moved from five models to nine. Spread across three different series. We have the Q950, the Q900 and the Q800. Screen sizes ranging from 55 inch up to 98 inch. Below that we have a full range. As you can imagine of 4k so again going from Q95 down to Q60 we've actually. Expanded the QLED lineup and we've increased the large screen offering so. By that I mean 75 inch and above by roughly 50% year-on-year as that's one. Of the markets which you know we're seeing the biggest growth opportunities. Then below QLED we have our crystal UHD models as well. They will be made up of. Three series with screen sizes ranging from 43 inch all the way up to 85. So let's focus on the 8K QLED for the moment because I think that is going to be your. Main push for 2020. What are the differences between the Q950, the Q900. And also the Q800. Well, Q950 is quite a special model. I mean, just to define it as an 8K TV. Probably sells it a little bit short. I mean, there's been a huge revolution in terms of design. So we have something which we are calling. The Infinity Screen. So essentially what we have is a 99% screen to body ratio. We've removed not only the bezel,. But also the black matrix,. Which would normally go around the picture. So you are seeing predominantly screen. That's what you're seeing. And what that helps to do is create. That immersive viewing experience. On top of that, sound has been a huge focus for us in our 2020 lineup. What we're doing is we're actually integrating speakers on the top, side and bottom of the televisions. With that, we have lots of opportunities for new technology. As an example, object tracking sound is a big focus for us. What we'll be able to do is any source material which is fed into the television,. Using our algorithm, we'll be able to understand where the action is being placed on the screen. And we'll match the sound output to the action. What that will give you then is a more realistic viewing experience with combining both picture and sound. So that's probably the main selling points of the 8K model. Of course the 8K processor has also developed year on year. We're going now into a kind of machine learning system. So the TV is constantly learning how to upscale. What's the best way to optimize any picture which has not been created in native 8K resolution,. Be that full HD or 4K. Upscale that to 8k using all of the learning of everything that's gone on before any pictures it. Has in the database plus any pictures that have been fed into the tv since the tv has been you. Know in in working production so those are the main features that we'll be driving from 8k point. Of view of course there's all of the other great pitch quality functionalities on top of that. Direct full array high peak brightness so hdr continues to be an area of the market where we. Where we look to lead and excel yeah i would say those are probably the the main focus for us. In terms of the 8K lineup. Then moving down the lineup,. So the Q900 features a lot of the same specification as the 950,. Slight design alterations,. So that will be in a different kind of place of the market. And then we have the Q800,. Which is our entry model into 8K for 2020. Screen sizes, again, from 55-inch up to 98. Again, featuring a lot of the same technologies. That I've just mentioned. We have the anti-reflection screen. This was a big functionality for us in 2019 so it's something we look to to focus on again for. 2020 so there what we're looking at is how we're controlling ambient light which is you know. Reflecting onto the screen how we're managing to channel that so that consumers are getting. The best level of picture performance regardless of how light is being pushed onto the tv that's. A big functionality for us to talk about sound also important on the q800 multiple speaker. Implementation we're looking for a lot of harmony this year between our tv products and our q. Soundbar products as well. One of the ways we're going to do that is with the. Feature called Q-Symphony. So what we'll be able to do when adding a Q-Series. Soundbar to a compatible QLED TV, we will actually keep the top and side. Speakers open so they will still be working in conjunction with the soundbar. So you know normally when you attach a soundbar to the TV it automatically cuts. Off the television's sound output. We're actually looking to harness the. Television's additional speakers in conjunction with that soundbar to create. That surround sound cinematic experience. So those are all new functionalities. That we're going to be talking about. When we talk about 8K,. HDMI 2.1 is at the forefront of my thoughts. What is the status of HDMI support. Across your TV lineup,. Not only for the 8K models,. But also 4K models? So we have varying levels of support for HDMI 2.1,. Varying from supporting full specification,. And then throughout the lineup,. There are various levels of support,. Which go not just from our 8K models. Or even premium 4K models,. All the way down to what you consider to be our entry-level UHD offerings. So HDMI 2.1, we are covered for the functionalities which we need to be covered. And then for the flagship models, they will cover the entire specification. So I would like to be a bit more specific here because there are, as you said, various features of HDMI 2.1. So let's say 4K at 120Hz, VRR, ALLM and also eARC, which models in your 2020 lineup will support them? So the 8K models will support the full specification. As we go down the range, we will probably start to remove certain functionalities,. But we will continue to keep eARC, we will continue to keep auto low latency,. We will continue to keep variable refresh rate. So what we've done is really reviewed at each part of the range,. What features and functionalities are essential for that. You know that product offering versus what the market expects and that's kind of how we've made. Our mind up on what support because you know there's always that that consideration of cost. Versus performance so I'm pretty confident that any HDMI 2.1 specification which has to be covered. Is covered at the relevant parts of the range. Talking of which ERC support for the 2019 Q90R. What is the status on that? Yeah so there's been a little bit of a delay on that but it is something. That we're very conscious of and we continue to work on that in the background so i'm hoping that. We're going to have something we'll be able to communicate soon but nothing's changed with. Regards to our original plan we will be supporting and updating as we uh as we you know originally. Said again i think this year you are not supporting dolby vision what would be your rationale behind. It you know i've probably answered this question about uh about a million times over the uh over. The years not just for samsung but for uh for others as well um i think our strategy um really. Comes down to focusing on the inherent capabilities of the product. There's this kind of myth, I think, in the industry where by supporting a functionality. Like the one you mentioned, that it automatically guarantees a certain level of performance,. That it makes a TV premium. It really doesn't. A TV is only as good as what its inherent capabilities are. I mean, there are TVs now which claim that functionality and achieve levels of brightness. Of, what, 200, 300 nits. Where we've been focusing on is really industry-leading HDR performance. And then we have fantastic tone mapping you know our own proprietary system as well so. That's where the focus is now we're still pushing HDR HDR 10 plus is still compatibility which will. Be in our entire lineup in 2020 but yeah so we'll continue to focus on that inherent capability. And of course you can imagine we are still monitoring all developments which are happening. In the market both from a hardware and content side yeah and that's that's you know that approach. Is how we'll continue going forward. Clearly my channel is very focused on enthusiasm and picture quality but Samsung also offers. A range of lifestyle displays as well. Would you like to expand on that for 2020? Yeah, I mean it's been hugely successful in the previous two years. So we've had the Frame and we've had Serif coming in a various range of sizes and colours. And what we're finding now is there's a consumer market out there that really wants to have. A product which is more personable to them, something that they can customise, that better. Reflects them as an individual. So we will expand those lineups in 2020. We'll add a. Couple of new screen sizes to the frame that will come in 32 inch 75 as well as the current. Screen sizes we offer. Serif will keep the screen sizes but we'll have new colors. We'll. Have cloud white and cotton blue. And then the Serif is something that we're introducing. Which is very unique indeed. It's a TV which can move between vertical and horizontal orientations. We're already selling this in Korea. It's selling phenomenally well and we believe there's. A great market opportunity here in Europe, you know, with a very targeted audience, you. Know, the kind of consumers that are flicking through social media maybe more than they're. Watching standard television. So that's the TV that we're going to be focusing for them. And when we go down the range, I'm seeing this technology called dual LED on some of. The entry-level QLEDs, such as the Q60 and Q70, I believe. Can you explain what it does? What are its benefits? Yeah so I mean a lot of the performances that we're talking about. At the moment are reserved for the top end of the range but in that kind of core segment. What we've noticed with the Edge LED products I mean traditionally we've been using cool LEDs. You get a little bit of oversaturation there particularly in the blue tones so dual LED what. We've done is we've been able to line up the LEDs using a combination of cool and warm. And then by using that by having that flexibility to tone the picture up or down we're able to. Deliver much more realistic contrast ratios and be more specific to the content that's. Being displayed on the screen. So this is on the QLED models, Q60, Q70, but it's also found on the frame. And I think on the frame it's really visible. When you put a certain artwork on the screen which has a warm color palette, by utilizing. The, you know, increasing the level of warmth from the LED, I think you get a much more. Realistic picture versus the original content intention. So again, it's just another way that we've taken our current products, which are performing. And selling very well and just move them on one gear by listening to feedback from the. Market and from our consumers. If I had to ask you to sum up the key advantages of Samsung's sets versus your competitors,. What would you say? I mean, firstly, what I would say is, you know, it's a very competitive market and I. Think all manufacturers are really bringing some fantastic technologies. I think the difference I've noticed personally since joining Samsung, you know, I've been. In product development now for 12 years. The performance that Samsung can deliver in multiple. Environments, I think is really industry leading. Now, you can put TVs on test benches and you can. Turn the lights off and you can talk about which TVs can achieve the darkest levels or the best. Contrast. But the majority of consumers are not really watching TVs in those kind of environments. You know, how does your TV perform when your curtains are open and light is streaming in? Is your TV providing you with the applications which are giving you the most desired content? You know we're coming out and saying okay from launch in march we all support disney plus it'll. Be a key application which you will find on all samsung televisions you know those are the kind of. Must-have experiences and must-have functionalities our consumers are telling us that they want. And that's really at the core of our product development thanks a lot craig really appreciate. You talking to us from what i've actually seen at this forum i think you again have an amazingly. Comprehensive array of products to suit all types of requirements and budget and. I wish you and your company all the best for 2020. Thank you very much and all the. Best to you and all of your followers as well. Thank you.
